summary: DeepSeek-V4.1 computes attention in BF16 and logits in FP32 like the reference
compatibility: VLLM_DS41_ATTENTION_COMPUTE=auto restores the previous tuner choice (FP8 or BF16 per plan); --hf-overrides '{"head_dtype": "model"}' restores BF16 logits. Output token streams change within numerical noise.
details: b12x V4.1 sparse attention is pinned to BF16 arithmetic (BF16 Q, KV dequantized to BF16, BF16 P, FP32 accumulation) instead of the tuner's FP8 internals, which carried about 3% relative error against DeepSeek's reference sparse_attn. Measured throughput on 4x RTX PRO 6000 is unchanged.
VLLM_DS41_ATTENTION_COMPUTE=reference also runs decode rows single-pass, reproducing the reference kernel bit for bit at up to 17% lower low-concurrency decode speed.

On RTX PRO / SM120, DeepSeek-V4.1 (target and DSpark draft) defaults to head_dtype=float32: the LM head accumulates into FP32 logits instead of rounding them to BF16 steps of up to 1/8, matching the reference head. Measured decode speed is unchanged.
head_dtype=float32 no longer rejects runtime-quantized LM heads (for example the optional NVFP4 DSpark drafter and Markov heads): their logits are widened to FP32.
